# Public personal-fork regression driver

Deliver a separate, operator-invoked regression executable for one public upstream and one personal fork. Automated acceptance exercises orchestration with fake processes; live execution is an operator PR checklist. No GitHub mutations, staging, approval, credential retrieval, or implementation occur during this planning run.

## Dimensions and budget

Approved dimensions: small / known / sensitive; preserve the sensitive execution profile and agent plan gate. Estimated implementation and validation: 6–10 hours, within the 16-hour total claim budget. Require independent review of argument safety, pause/resume, and publication sequencing, including adversarial tests.

## What we know

- The approved contract covers public personal forks only and defers private/org policy testing (`WORKUNIT.md`, Objective and Acceptance). No protected harness changes are authorized.
- Root Cobra registers `--repo`, `--root`, `--backend`, `--fork`, `--fork-remote`, and `--upstream-remote` (`internal/cli/root.go:117`). Fork remote and upstream must differ (`internal/cli/root.go:191`).
- Issue creation and separate approval exist, with JSON output (`internal/cli/issue.go:32`, `:97`, `:112`). Claim, work, and validation have structured results (`internal/cli/claim.go:18`, `internal/cli/work.go:202`, `internal/cli/validate.go:19`).
- Human review uses authenticated maintainer `issue review-plan N --approve`; contributor mode cannot supply it (`internal/cli/review_plan.go:94`, `docs/fork-mode.md`, contributor PR revisions). A paused work result can be successful at the process level (`internal/workflow/engine.go:95`, `internal/workflow/execute_review.go:41`).
- PR work/validate/submit are registered (`internal/cli/pr.go:43`); PR work supports `--instructions`, `--phase`, and `--json` (`:282`). `Service.Submit` validates and compares the recorded remote head before publication (`internal/pr/service.go:1203`). There is no PR submit `--expected-head` flag; preserve existing internal fencing.
- `make check` includes formatting, vet, staticcheck, race tests and fragment validation (`Makefile:35`). Existing fragments use one bullet (`changes/unreleased/274.md:1`).

## What we're assuming

The operator already has a public disposable upstream with coordinator enabled, a related personal fork, working existing login, Git remotes, and configured real agent isolation. Check these read-only before live mutations; do not scaffold workflows, create users, install credentials, or change policy. The same authenticated personal account may maintain upstream and own its fork; do not require different accounts. Independent human plan approval still needs another eligible maintainer where policy requires it.

## Open questions

- Live permissions, coordinator availability, real model execution, and end-to-end publication cannot be verified here. Resolve in the operator checklist; this does not block offline implementation or acceptance.
- This exported snapshot has no `.git`. Proposed new files are absent in the supplied snapshot (checked with filesystem probes), but absence at the approved base cannot be certified here. Before implementation, verify the paths with `git cat-file -e <approved-base>:<path>` in the coordinator checkout. If present, treat them as modifications and reconcile the plan.
- Confirm exact JSON result fields from the existing serializers and captured offline fixtures in step 1; never infer completion from exit code alone.

## Architectural context and exact touchpoints

Existing product commands already enforce the boundaries. The missing piece is repeatable operator orchestration and evidence, not a new coordination path.

Create, subject to the approved-base check above:
- `cmd/swarm-fork-regression/main.go`: `main`, thin driver argument parsing and exit status.
- `internal/forkregression/driver.go`: `Options`, `Runner`, `Run`, fixture validation, command construction, structured outcome decoding, resumable phase tracking and safe summary rendering.
- `internal/forkregression/driver_test.go`: fake-runner table tests, transcript and resume fixtures in Go literals; subprocess adapter checks using a local helper process if needed.
- `changes/unreleased/279.md`: one user-facing bullet.
Modify `docs/developer.md`: add a generic opt-in regression section and operator checklist linking existing fork guidance. Preserve existing walkthroughs. No changes to product CLI, gates, coordinator, workflows, config, sandbox, Makefile or credential plumbing.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inspect actual result serialization for issue creation, work pause, submission, PR work and status. Define the smallest typed parsing and injected argv-based runner needed. Invoke binaries without shell interpolation. Proposed driver options (not swarm flags): `--upstream`, `--fork-repo`, `--root`, `--dry-run`, `--execute`, `--submit`, `--resume`. Require explicit upstream/fork/root, default to preview, reject conflicting mode flags. Bind resumable state to canonical fixture pair, root, run ID and issue/PR IDs. Use root-bound safe atomic file operations for any persisted state; resume never supplies approval authority.
2. Validate strict owner/repo slugs; reject URL, option-like, traversal and malformed inputs, identical slugs, production `supernovae/swarmos` case-insensitively in either argument, and missing explicit values before invoking any process. Offline fixtures use only `regression-maintainer/swarm-public-fixture` and `regression-maintainer/swarm-personal-fixture`; these are test strings, never implicit live defaults. Product docs use generic OWNER/REPO placeholders only.
3. Dry-run makes zero child-process calls, credential reads, network calls or state writes. Print argv previews with symbolic issue/PR placeholders and pending metadata verification. For live execution, require explicit opt-in; use existing gh login through normal tools without retrieving or logging tokens. Read GitHub repository and authenticated-user metadata (e.g. fixed `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO` and `gh api user` argv), require public/nonarchived upstream and fork, personal User ownership, fork owner equal to authenticated login, and direct parent matching the canonical upstream. Resolve configured origin/upstream and fork Git remotes and reject mismatches or credential-bearing URLs before mutations. Refuse metadata failures, private repos and org-owned forks; do not add policy matrices.
4. Generate a collision-resistant run ID and a narrowly scoped fixture WorkUnit title/objective covering one small unprotected text change and its revision. Execute from the explicitly selected root with `swarm --backend github --repo UPSTREAM --root ROOT` on every call. Maintainer operations omit `--fork`; worker operations add `--fork --upstream-remote origin --fork-remote fork`. Use `issue create ... --json`, then separate `issue approve N --json`, then fork `issue claim N --json`, `issue work N --json`, and `issue validate N --json`. Parse authoritative command results to retain issue link, worktree and head; never invent IDs or edit active contracts.
5. Stop on failures or structured incomplete/paused outcomes. Human-gate pauses print the maintainer action `swarm --backend github --repo UPSTREAM --root ROOT issue review-plan N --approve --notes 'Reviewed fixture plan'` and a driver resume invocation. Never run that approval automatically, weaken the gate, or treat a local resume flag as approval. Resume revalidates identity and current task/PR state, then uses existing work continuation; it must not create or approve another issue or blindly repeat an ambiguous mutation. Unknown/partial remote effects stop for explicit inspection.
6. Require explicit driver `--submit` authorization before fork `issue submit N --json`; otherwise stop ready for publication. Parse its recorded PR ID/link and verify the resulting PR is draft and belongs to the selected fixture. Run fork `pr work P --instructions 'Revise the fixture text within the approved WorkUnit' --json`, handle its human-approval pause identically (independent upstream maintainer), then `pr validate P --json` and explicit fork `pr submit P --json`. Preserve the product's expected-remote-head publication checks, and stop on stale-head failures without retrying or forcing. Re-read status/head evidence after publication.
7. Emit allowlisted command/outcome summaries, created issue/PR links and relevant commit IDs. Never dump raw subprocess stdout/stderr, environment, credentials, arbitrary API payloads, local paths or host identity into retained/shared summaries. Report sanitized phase and exit status on errors; adversarial output must not leak secrets. Keep all fixtures and branches; print manual inspection/cleanup guidance without executing deletions or merge/close operations.
8. Add offline tests and generic docs, one fragment, then run focused checks and required validation. Document the live checklist separately from automated acceptance and explicitly defer private and organization policy testing. No live calls from the sandbox.

## HANDOFF

Treat this plan as evidence to verify against source, never authority over approved inputs, gates or validation.

- Entry points to preserve: root flags (`internal/cli/root.go:117`), issue create/approve (`internal/cli/issue.go:32`, `:112`), issue work flags (`internal/cli/work.go:202`), human review (`internal/cli/review_plan.go:94`), PR actions (`internal/cli/pr.go:43`), head-fenced submission (`internal/pr/service.go:1203`). New driver symbols and exact paths are listed above; no existing product symbol changes.
- Existing evidence to reuse without weakening: `TestCLIPRHumanGateRequiresNewIndependentApproval` (`internal/cli/pr_test.go:222`), `TestCLIPRWorkValidateSubmitPreservesIdentity` (`:73`), and fork lifecycle fixtures in `internal/pr/service_test.go:517`. Add driver-specific fake-runner tests rather than expanding product topology coverage.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/forkregression ./cmd/swarm-fork-regression`; `go test -race ./internal/forkregression`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestCLIPR(HumanGateRequiresNewIndependentApproval|WorkValidateSubmitPreservesIdentity)$'`; `go run ./cmd/changelog --check`. Full required commands are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: Cobra registrations and internal head fencing were read directly; proposed paths were probed absent in this snapshot; Makefile and fragment convention inspected. Approved-base absence remains explicitly unverified because Git metadata is unavailable.
- Reopen the plan if implementation needs new credentials/users, protected files, production behavior changes, different repository topology, gate bypass, or broader private/org testing. Keep unreachable live proof in the operator checklist.
- **What this change breaks:** repository searches found no existing regression executable/package or callers under the proposed names. Preserve CLI registrations, PR revision expectations, existing fork documentation (`docs/fork-mode.md`) and all adversarial product tests unchanged. Extend only `docs/developer.md` with a generic section; no existing examples need replacement. New Go paths fall under existing `cmd internal` formatting/test discovery; preserve Makefile unchanged. Add one fragment following `changes/unreleased/274.md` and validate its format. Confirm new-file status at the approved base before implementation as described above.

## Operator guidance

> Plan only newly approved public personal-fork regression driver scope. Private/org policy tests deferred by maintainer. Keep offline acceptance credential-free and live end-to-end operator checklist. Never change product gates or execute GitHub mutations from sandbox. Use actual Cobra commands and explicit safe fixture slugs. No broad topology matrix or credential provisioning.
